newsitem.title: RUSSIA: St Petersburg plans Eurobond issue through Salomon.
newsitem.headline: St Petersburg plans Eurobond issue through Salomon.

text.p: Russia's second city of St Petersburg is planning to issue at least $300 million worth of dollar or mark Eurobonds through U.S. investment bank Salomon Bros, the city's finance committee said on Monday.
A bill to be submitted to city deputies in the first half of November calls for the issue of bonds, which would run for three to five years. It was not clear when the bonds would be issued.

The Eurobonds would be issued in London and listed in London or Frankfurt after a roadshow in Germany, Switzerland and Britain. The bonds would be targeted at investors in Germany, Switzerland and South-East Asia.
The city intends to get a credit-rating to lower the cost of the bonds, but will launch them if necessary without a rating. It envisages annual interest of 11-12 percent on the paper.
St Petersburg governor Vladimir Yakovlev will meet Salomon Bros officials in London on Tuesday to discuss the issue, the finance committee's press service said.

St Petersburg already has a prolific municipal note programme on the Russian domestic market, and in April mandated Salomon to sell up to $200 million of short-term municipal paper to foreign investors.

The Russian Federation is preparing its debut Eurobond in November, for which it has received speculative ratings, and the city of Moscow and region of Sverdlovsk have also outlined plans to issue Eurobonds.
